input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# GA-readiness assessment for Llama Stack

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: no systematic GA-readiness
assessment of Llama Stack has been done, and TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets. The assessment inventories the gaps between current Tech
Preview quality and the GA bar across API stability, upgrade paths, scale
limits, and error handling, and produces the definitive GA scope that the
stability and hardening work is planned from. Until this assessment lands, the
size of the graduation work is only an estimate.

## Scope

- Inventory API stability gaps on the published API surface (current
  versioning state, unintentional breaking changes between TP releases,
  deprecation exposure).
- Assess the upgrade paths from the last two TP releases, identifying breaks
  and missing migration steps.
- Identify scale limits (concurrency, throughput, resource ceilings) relative
  to the GA bar.
- Assess error handling coverage and behavior on the published surfaces.
- Consolidate TP feedback scattered across support tickets and validate it
  against the current codebase.
- Produce the definitive GA scope: an enumerated gap inventory with severity,
  each gap classified as GA-blocking or deferrable, with a recommended
  remediation approach at a level the implementing team can plan from.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A GA-readiness report exists covering all four enumerated dimensions (API
  stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), each with
  enumerated, specific findings.
- TP feedback from support tickets is consolidated and either confirmed
  against the codebase or explicitly marked unconfirmed.
- A definitive GA scope is produced that classifies every identified gap as
  GA-blocking or deferrable.
- Every GA-blocking gap carries a recommended remediation approach sufficient
  for implementation planning.
- The report distinguishes measured/verified findings from reported-but-
  unconfirmed ones.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): "A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current
  TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error
  handling), producing the definitive GA scope." This epic is that assessment.

# Llama Stack API stability and GA hardening

## Description

This epic delivers the GA-bar quality work for Llama Stack: the published API
surface carries a stability guarantee (versioned APIs, a deprecation policy,
and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases), and the GA-blocking
quality gaps identified by the GA-readiness assessment are remediated. The
scope of the hardening work is defined by the assessment's definitive GA
scope; this epic is planned as an estimate until that assessment lands.

## Scope

- Introduce API versioning on the published Llama Stack API surface.
- Define the deprecation policy covering the published API surface, authored
  together with the versioning scheme it governs.
- Build and test the upgrade path from each of the last two TP releases.
- Remediate the GA-blocking findings of the GA-readiness assessment (error
  handling, scale limits, and other assessment-identified gaps), per the
  definitive GA scope.
- Keep the existing Konflux build pipeline green throughout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published APIs are versioned and the versioning scheme is documented.
- A deprecation policy covering the published API surface is defined and
  published.
- Upgrade from each of the last two TP releases is exercised by automated
  tests and passes.
- Every GA-blocking finding from the GA-readiness assessment is remediated,
  or explicitly deferred with recorded rationale in the GA scope.
- The existing Konflux build pipeline remains green with all changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): "Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned
  APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP
  releases." The deprecation policy is authored here rather than in the
  documentation epic because it is part of the same stability-guarantee
  deliverable on the same API surface — the policy expresses the versioning
  decisions this epic makes.
- Implements the remediation half of HLR-1's output: the GA-blocking findings
  from the GA-readiness assessment are closed here.

# Supported TrustyAI guardrails integration for Llama Stack distributions

## Description

This epic promotes the TrustyAI safety guardrails integration for Llama Stack
from an experimental flag to a supported, documented integration qualified for
GA distributions. TrustyAI itself is a GA component; the work here is
qualifying, enabling, and documenting its guardrails integration as a
supported part of Llama Stack GA distributions.

## Scope

- Qualify the TrustyAI guardrails integration against GA support criteria
  (functional validation end-to-end against a Llama Stack distribution).
- Enable the integration as supported in Llama Stack distributions —
  configuration-level enablement, not an experimental opt-in flag.
- Validate guardrails behavior end-to-end with a running Llama Stack
  distribution, covering the failure and misconfiguration paths a supported
  integration must handle.
- Document the supported integration: configuration, capabilities, and support
  boundaries. This documentation is part of the integration deliverable (it
  defines what "supported" means for this integration); it is distinct from
  the broader Llama Stack GA documentation uplift.
- Coordinate with the Llama Stack distribution owners on enablement defaults
  for GA distributions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The guardrails integration is available in GA Llama Stack distributions
  without an experimental opt-in flag.
- The integration is validated end-to-end against a Llama Stack distribution,
  including error and misconfiguration behavior, with results recorded.
- Documentation for the supported integration exists, covering configuration,
  capabilities, and support boundaries.
- The supported integration can be disabled via supported configuration
  without code changes (rollback for the replaced experimental-flag behavior).
- The existing build pipeline for the changed repositories remains green.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): "Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions."

# Dashboard Llama Stack management enabled by default for entitled clusters

## Description

This epic removes the Tech Preview opt-in gate so that the Dashboard enables
Llama Stack management by default on entitled clusters. Today the management
experience sits behind a TP opt-in; for GA it becomes a default-on,
entitlement-gated capability.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard's Llama Stack management default from opt-in to
  enabled, using the Dashboard's existing per-component feature-flag and
  defaults configuration mechanism.
- Remove the Tech Preview opt-in gate for Llama Stack management.
- Gate the default enablement on cluster entitlement: enabled on entitled
  clusters, hidden or disabled elsewhere.
- Update captions, labels, and references that fall out of this change (e.g.,
  removing TP designations on the management surfaces) — incidental touch-ups
  only, no new content authored here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster, Llama Stack management surfaces in the Dashboard
  with no user opt-in action.
- On a non-entitled cluster, Llama Stack management surfaces are not enabled.
- The default enablement is controlled through the Dashboard's existing
  configuration mechanism so it can be reverted without code changes
  (rollback for the replaced opt-in-gate behavior).
- The existing Dashboard test suite and build pipeline remain green.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P1): "The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for
  entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate)."

## Notes

- **Release-timing coordination:** the default-on management experience is
  intended to ship as part of the Llama Stack GA graduation, not before it.
  This is a release-composition matter — coordinate the release timing of
  this change with the Llama Stack GA release planning so the default-on
  Dashboard experience lands with (not ahead of) the GA graduation. It is
  deliberately not a DAG dependency: this epic's implementation is complete
  and independently testable regardless of GA timing, so it blocks on
  nothing and only the GA documentation epic consumes its outcome.

# Llama Stack GA documentation and production support posture

## Description

This epic uplifts Llama Stack documentation to GA standards and publishes the
production support posture required for GA: documented SLO targets, backport
policy, and supported configuration matrix, plus migration notes from the Tech
Preview releases. It is authored after the implementation work so the
documentation and support commitments describe what was actually built and
validated.

## Scope

Content outline:

- **Support posture documentation**
  - SLO targets for the production support of Llama Stack
  - Backport policy
  - Supported configuration matrix, consistent with the configurations
    validated during the GA hardening work
- **GA-standard documentation uplift**
  - Uplift of Llama Stack documentation to GA standards (accuracy, coverage,
    completeness relative to the GA feature set)
  - Migration notes from Tech Preview releases, covering the tested upgrade
    path from the last two TP releases
  - Removal of Tech Preview designations and caveats that GA no longer
    excuses

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documented SLO targets are published for Llama Stack production support.
- The backport policy is published.
- The supported configuration matrix is published and is consistent with the
  configurations actually validated during the GA hardening work.
- Migration notes from TP exist and cover the tested upgrade path from the
  last two TP releases.
- All documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented GA
  behavior (reviewed by the teams that implemented the stability, guardrails,
  and Dashboard work).
- Documentation content is validated for accuracy against the platform
  architecture context.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): "Production support posture is in place: documented SLO
  targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix."
- HLR-6 (P2, bundled): "Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including
  migration notes from TP." Bundled with HLR-3 here because both are Llama
  Stack documentation authoring on the same doc surface for the same team and
  work-product type; splitting them would produce two docs epics over the
  same surface with an artificial serialization edge, and the migration notes
  and support posture publish together as one GA documentation set.

Strategy status: Refinement Done. Strategy priority: Critical (frontmatter).
All three affected components (Llama Stack, TrustyAI, Dashboard) have
architecture-context files and are in the platform; no onboarding chains are
needed (Llama Stack is already Konflux-onboarded per its context file).

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9014-E001 | GA-readiness assessment for Llama Stack | Investigation | RHOAI GenAI | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9014-E002 | Llama Stack API stability and GA hardening | Implementation | RHOAI GenAI | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9014-E003 | Supported TrustyAI guardrails integration for Llama Stack distributions | Implementation | TrustyAI | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9014-E004 | Dashboard Llama Stack management enabled by default for entitled clusters | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9014-E001 GA-readiness assessment] --> E002[RHAISTRAT-9014-E002 API stability and hardening]
    E002 --> E005[RHAISTRAT-9014-E005 GA docs and support posture]
    E003[RHAISTRAT-9014-E003 TrustyAI guardrails integration] --> E005
    E004[RHAISTRAT-9014-E004 Dashboard default enablement] --> E005
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge / non-edge | Rule | Rationale |
|-----------------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Investigation edge (Rule 3) | The strategy's only open question states the GA scope depends on the assessment — until it lands, the size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate. The assessment's answer changes what E002 does, so E002 is a true gate (`gated_by=E001`, `gate_failure_impact.action=rewrite`). Outcomes are an unbounded gap inventory (not ≤3 bounded possibilities), so no conditional branch epics; the gate is expressed via `gate_failure_impact` on E002. |
| E002 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | GA documentation and the support posture (SLO targets, backport policy, supported configuration matrix, migration notes) describe what was built; blocked by every Implementation epic. |
| E003 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Same — the GA documentation set must reflect the supported guardrails integration. |
| E004 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Same — the GA documentation set must reflect the default-on Dashboard management experience. |
| E001 ∥ E003 (non-edge) | Rule 14 / Step 3 decision rule | The assessment's scope is enumerated as API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling — it does not cover the TrustyAI guardrails integration. Whether guardrails are promoted to a supported integration does not depend on the assessment outcome, so no gate. |
| E001 ∥ E004 (non-edge) | Rule 14 / Step 3 decision rule | Dashboard default enablement is not part of the assessment's enumerated dimensions; the answer does not change what the Dashboard epic does. |
| E002 ∥ E003 (non-edge) | Rule 14 | Different components, different teams, different repos (llama-stack midstream vs. trustyai-service-operator); no shared build artifacts. The guardrails integration qualifies against the current distribution and does not build against the API-stability work. |
| E002 ∥ E004 (non-edge) | Rules 14/15 | Different components and repos; the Dashboard change is a feature-flag/default flip on an existing management surface, not work that builds against the API stability deliverables. Release timing coordination (default-on ships with GA) is a release-composition matter, noted as a coordination note in E004's Notes section, not a DAG dependency. |
| E003 ∥ E004 (non-edge) | Rule 14 | Different components, teams, and repos; fully independent. |

**Rule 19 considered and not applied:** the strategy is a GA graduation
program, not a safety-critical implementation — the guardrails work (HLR-4)
qualifies an existing TrustyAI integration (TrustyAI itself is Stable/GA per
its architecture-context file) rather than building new guardrails, sandboxing,
